newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM aims to expand into E.Africa.
newsitem.headline: KLM aims to expand into E.Africa.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV is aiming to expand into eastern Africa following the open skies agreement between the Netherlands and Kenya announced last week, a KLM spokesman told Reuters.
KLM Cargo is interested in using the east African network of Kenya Airways, he said. The African airline operates Boeing 737s and smaller aircraft in the region.
The Dutch airline has a 26 percent stake in Kenya Airways and has been operating services with the African carrier since November 1996.

The two operate joint services between Amsterdam Schiphol Airport and Nairobi. KLM operates three weekly McDonnell Douglas MD-11 flights and Kenya Airways flies an Airbus A3100 three times a week under a code-share agreement. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
